speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long this wound on your right lower leg has been present and how it started? Also, do you have any history of diabetes, venous insufficiency, or peripheral artery disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound have a well-defined border, and do you notice any brownish discoloration or hardening of the skin around it? I would also like to know if the pain worsens when you elevate your leg or improves with dependent positioning.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound exude a significant amount of fluid, and is the surrounding skin warm and red? I would also like to know if you see any visible varicose veins or if the skin feels thick and leathery to the touch.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of DVT, chronic swelling, and family history strongly suggests post-thrombotic syndrome leading to a venous stasis ulcer. REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial_Index.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal ABI, arterial disease is unlikely, so I will proceed with imaging to assess for venous pathology. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms chronic venous insufficiency with reflux and obstruction, which is the underlying cause of your wound. I am now confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer
